description_full: Trimble Inc. offers technology solutions and platform that enable office professionals and field workers to connect workflows and industry lifecycles in North America, Europe, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. The company provides architecture and interior design; building information modeling, engineering, and virtual design and construction; and construction and owner software products. It also offers field and office software for estimating and job cost management, and project design and visualization; software for 3D design and data sharing; systems to guide and control construction equipment, such as excavators, bulldozers, wheel loaders, motor graders, and paving equipment; systems to monitor, track, and manage assets, equipment, and workers; and software to facilitate the management of the construction process and for sharing and communication of data in real time. In addition, it provides positioning services comprising VRSNow; CenterPoint RTX; FieldPoint RTX; Rangepoint RTX; ViewPoint RTX; and Trimble xFill services. Further, it offers transportation and logistics solutions for shippers, carriers, retailers, and intermediaries, such as carrier transportation management software (TMS) and maintenance solutions to manage core transportation operations and maintenance workflows; transporeon solutions to provide a cloud-based ecosystem that manages the transportation lifecycle from freight sourcing and procurement through transport execution, dock and yard management, and auditing; and MAPS, a mapping and routing solutions that provide the industry standard for truck-specific routing, mileage, and navigation. It sells its technology solutions directly to end users and through software integrations. The company was formerly known as Trimble Navigation Limited and changed its name to Trimble Inc. in October 2016. Trimble Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Westminster, Colorado.

financial_summary: Trimble Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $12.8B market cap on $3.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 54% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $361M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.91× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.0×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 10pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 22% over the past year excluding the latest month.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $18.10 (margin of safety -207%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 11%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $12.08 to $27.27 (P10-P90).
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/E 13.8 vs 27.4, richer on P/FCF 35.3 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 34% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 11 covering analysts target $74.18 on average, 33% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.2%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have been steady (CV 0.23).
It runs a 54% gross margin and converts 10% of revenue into free cash flow, or 6% after stock compensation.
ROE of 7% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.6x equity multiplier).
It spends 17.6% of revenue on R&D and 4.1% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.4x net debt to EBITDA ($253.4M of cash against $1.4B of debt), with interest covered 8.0x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.3, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 56% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -0.8% over 3 years, 2.6% over 5 years and 4.6% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -10.1% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.08 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 56% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 11%.
Capex runs only 0.1x depreciation (0.7% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 9, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.4%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (5 sales, net $1.9M sold).
It returns 6.8% a year to shareholders (6.8% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 11,500 employees, each generates about $312K of revenue, 0.8x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 7.0% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $31K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.6M (12x revenue per employee).
